x: India joined the US-led Minerals Security Partnership in June 2023 (I correct), and the MMDR Amendment Act 2023 lets only the Centre auction mining leases and composite licences for the 24 critical and strategic minerals in Part D of the First Schedule (III correct). II is wrong: India is wholly or heavily import-dependent for many of its 30 critical minerals (lithium, cobalt, nickel …).
source: Ministry of Mines, MMDR Amendment Act 2023 (mines.gov.in); PIB, India joins MSP (June 2023); notes row 44 sub 6

x: Anantapur (Ananthapuramu): in 2025 Tata Power Renewable (after its March 2025 MoU with NREDCAP) tied up with Suzlon for a 700 MW, Rs 6,000 crore wind project there; Anantapur is AP's main wind belt, not Guntur, Visakhapatnam or Krishna.

Only III: Rajasthan has iron ore (Nathara-ki-Pal, Udaipur). I is wrong because State Governments auction non-coal mineral blocks under the MMDR Amendment 2015; II is wrong because AP (Ramagiri, Chigargunta–Bisanatham) and Jharkhand (Lawa, Parasi) have gold mines.
source: PMF H&E Geography 03 p.9 (Nathara-ki-Pal); NextGen Indian Geography 09 (gold); MMDR Amendment 2015 (mines.gov.in)

x: Chromite, kyanite and sillimanite are major minerals; bentonite was declared a minor mineral by the Centre's notification of 10 Feb 2015 (under Sec 3(e) of the MMDR Act), so II, III and IV only.
source: Ministry of Mines notification S.O. 423(E), 10 Feb 2015 (mines.gov.in); UPSC CSE 2020 official key (d)

x: Statement I is wrong: Section 15 of the MMDR Act empowers the State Governments to make rules for concessions of minor minerals. Statement II is right: under Section 3(e) the Centre may notify any mineral as a minor mineral.
source: MMDR Act 1957 (Sec 3(e), 15) and MMDR Amendment Acts 2015/2023 – mines.gov.in; app notes 4:44 sub 9

x: Only 2: a District Mineral Foundation (non-profit trust under the MMDR Amendment 2015, funded by miners) works for the interest of persons and areas affected by mining. Exploration is funded by NMET, and DMFs do not authorise licences.
source: MMDR Amendment Act 2015 Sec 9B (mines.gov.in); notes row 44 sub 7 (DMF, NMET)

x: The keyed set is andalusite (Sonbhadra holds ~91% of India's resources, Salaidih–Harwariya), pyrite and dolomite (Bari); uranium is usually credited to Lalitpur, so books drop it. The stem's 'metals' is loose – all four are minerals.
source: IBM, Uttar Pradesh mineral profile (ibm.gov.in/writereaddata/files/09232015123324Uttar Pradesh.pdf); AMD paper, IAEA CN-216 (179-Parihar.pdf)
dispute: Most books and keys: 2, 3, 4 (no uranium). Strictly AMD reports low-grade uranium mineralisation in Sonbhadra (Naktu–Kundabhati, found 1977-78), so all four occur (AMD paper, IAEA CN-216).
